campbell.title: Campbell City Council — October 20, 2026
campbell.summary: The agenda listed three items for the Campbell City Council: a proposed five-year lease agreement for a trailer, a request from the Pruneyard Shopping Center Association to change its permit timelines, and a presentation on VTA's strategic plan with a focus on its express lanes program. The agenda alone doesn't confirm whether these items were heard or what was decided.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a resolution to approve a 5-year lease agreement to procure a trailer (described in the agenda text as a thermoplastic military trailer).
The agenda listed an application from the Pruneyard Shopping Center Association to amend the Pruneyard Master Use Permit and extend deadlines for approval phasing.
The agenda listed a presentation on VTA's strategic plan as an agency and organization, with specific attention to the express lanes program.

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — October 21, 2026
saratoga.summary: The agenda for the October 21, 2026 Saratoga City Council meeting listed routine business such as approving past meeting minutes and bill-payment records, along with final approvals for two property splits. It also listed an annual update to the City Code and a proposal to start the process of creating a Climate Resilience District.
keyTopics: The agenda listed approval of the minutes from the September 30, 2026 special meeting and the October 7, 2026 regular meeting, plus acceptance of the vendor payment check registers dated 10/01/2026 and 10/08/2026.
The agenda listed final map approval for a two-lot split at 14860 Farwell Ave (parcel map application ULS25-0013).
The agenda listed final map approval for a two-lot split at 18510 Sobey Rd (parcel map application ULS25-0004).
The agenda listed a public hearing on the 2026 annual City Code update, including changes to rules on scheduling appeals and qualifications for City Commissioners.
The agenda listed two resolutions: one to establish a Climate Resilience District Task Force and one to begin the process of establishing a Climate Resilience District.

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — October 13, 2026
los-altos.summary: The agenda for the Los Altos City Council's October 13, 2026 meeting listed a mix of routine financial reports and approvals alongside a few policy items, including a new rebate program for home electrification and updated guidelines for below-market-rate housing. The council was also scheduled to review its handbook for city commissions and committees and receive an update on Ada's Cafe at the Community Center.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a resolution to amend the FY2026-27 budget with $78,000 from the general fund for a residential electrification rebate program.
The agenda listed a resolution to approve Below Market Rate (BMR) For-Sale and Rental Housing Guidelines, with a finding that the action is exempt from CEQA.

The agenda listed two project completion acceptances: the FY 2025-2026 on-call sanitary sewer spot repairs and CCTV inspection services, and the FY 2024-2025 Annual Streets Project built by O'Grady Paving, Inc.
The agenda listed a resolution to approve an updated Conflict of Interest Code for city staff and commissioners under the Political Reform Act of 1974.
The agenda included a review of the Commission and Committee Handbook, an update on Ada's Cafe at the Community Center, and the tentative council calendar and Housing Element implementation schedule.

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 20, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The agenda for the Los Gatos Town Council's October 20, 2026 meeting listed routine business items, including approving minutes from two October 6 meetings and receiving financial reports for August 2026. It also listed several items authorizing the Town Manager to sign or amend agreements, including one with Foster and Foster and a lease amendment.
keyTopics: Approval of minutes from the October 6, 2026 Town Council Special Meeting and regular Town Council Meeting
Receipt of the August 2026 Expenditure and Revenue Reports and the Monthly Financial and Investment Report for August 2026
Approval and ratification of the accounts payable check registers and payroll report
Authorization for the Town Manager to execute a first amendment with Foster and Foster
Authorization for the Town Manager to negotiate and execute an amendment to a lease, and to enter into a three-year agreement

san-jose.title: San José City Council — October 20, 2026
san-jose.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026 San José City Council meeting listed routine items such as meeting minutes, absence requests, and event approvals, along with reports from the City Manager and the Independent Police Auditor. It also listed several land-use items, including a street vacation, a proposed General Plan change, and two appeals involving development projects.
keyTopics: The agenda listed the 2025-2026 City Manager's Annual Report and the 2025 Independent Police Auditor Year End Report.
The agenda listed a District 9 end-of-term farewell celebration as a Council-sponsored special event, along with District 9 SAP funds for the Rotary Club of San Jose Foundation.
The agenda listed a Council District 5 proclamation, flag raising and lighting recognizing Taiwan Retrocession Day as a Council-sponsored special event.
The agenda listed a conditional vacation of a portion of Spring Street between Asbury Street and West Taylor Street.
The agenda listed an appeal of the in-fill exemption for a data center use at 300 Holger Way, along with appeals on environmental review and a site development permit for 470 West San Carlos Street.

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — October 20, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The published agenda for the October 20, 2026 Mountain View City Council meeting listed a 6:30 p.m. study session on interviews of applicants for the Environmental Planning Commission. The agenda also included standard notices on how residents can get meeting materials, request accessibility help, and submit comments to the Council.
keyTopics: Study session at 6:30 p.m. listed for interviews of applicants to the Environmental Planning Commission
Residents can email comments to city.council@mountainview.gov by 4:30 p.m. on the meeting date, with the agenda item number in the subject line
In-person speakers are asked to fill out a blue speaker card for each item they wish to speak on

Agenda materials are posted on the city's Legistar site and available at City Hall, the City Clerk's Office, and the Mountain View Library; accessibility assistance can be requested 48 hours ahead through the City Clerk's Office

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 6, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The agenda for the Sunnyvale City Council's October 6, 2026 meeting listed recognitions for the Little League Junior Division All-Stars and several awareness weeks, along with routine approvals and a few larger items for consideration. These included a new water-use rule on lawns, a proposed Service Worker Retention Ordinance, and public art for the Lakewood Park renovation.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a public hearing on an ordinance to ban using drinking-quality water to irrigate nonfunctional turf, to implement state law AB 1572, with the action described as exempt from CEQA.
The agenda listed discussion and possible action to introduce a Service Worker Retention Ordinance.
The agenda listed approval of public art for the Lakewood Park renovation.

The agenda listed a proposed $160,000 increase (to a new total of $385,000) and an extension through October 17, 2028 for an environmental consulting agreement with WSP USA Inc. supporting the SMaRT Station and Sunnyvale Landfill.

The agenda listed recognition of the 2026 Sunnyvale Little League Junior Division All-Stars, plus proclamations for Indigenous Peoples' Day, Friends of the Library Week, and Sunnyvale Stands United Against Hate Week.

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — October 20, 2026
cupertino.summary: The agenda for the Cupertino City Council's October 20, 2026 meeting lists a regular session at 6:45 PM, preceded by a special meeting at 5:45 PM, both at Community Hall with remote participation options. Items before the Council include a citywide update to the safety and health chapter of the General Plan, financing for an apartment project, a bridge design contract, and a proposed approach to leasing a city-owned commercial property.
keyTopics: The agenda listed proposed updates to the General Plan's Health and Safety chapter and related appendices (noise, geologic and seismic hazards), plus a new Health and Safety Background Report, applying citywide.
A public hearing was listed on conduit financing for The RISE Block 5 Apartments Project under the federal TEFRA process; the item was postponed from the October 6 meeting.

The consent calendar included a resolution to accept $850,000 in federal grant funds and award a design services agreement to Biggs Cardoza Associates, Inc. (not to exceed $1,278,700) for the McClellan Road Bridge Project.
The agenda listed a proposed approach for leasing the City-owned commercial property at 22100 Stevens Creek Boulevard as an action item.

Other consent items included a gymnastics classes and camps contract with Bay Aerials Gymnastics (up to $480,000, extendable to $800,000 over five years) and a proposed amendment to City Manager Tina Kapoor's employment agreement.

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara Neighborhood-University Relations Committee — October 19, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The agenda listed a special meeting of Santa Clara's Neighborhood University Relations Committee for October 19, 2026, at 6:00 pm in the City Hall Cafeteria, with the public also able to join by Zoom or phone. The agenda listed a discussion of neighborhood nuisance issues in private rental leases, along with routine items and updates from the city, Santa Clara University, and the police department.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a discussion of neighborhood nuisance topics in private property leases, with possible direction to staff to return with ways to share the committee's input with property owners in the Old Quad neighborhood.
The agenda listed updates from the Community Development Department, Santa Clara University, and the Police Department.
The agenda listed approval of the minutes from the May 18, 2026 meeting and the committee's 2027 meeting calendar.

Residents could participate in person, by Zoom, or by phone; written comments could be emailed to PlanningPublicComment@santaclaraca.gov by 12 p.m. the day of the meeting, and emails are not read aloud.

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — October 20, 2026
milpitas.summary: The agenda for the Milpitas City Council's October 20, 2026 meeting listed routine business such as calendars, minutes, and upcoming agenda previews, along with items on a park design contract, a presentation from the county's mosquito control district, and new names for city community gardens and a plaza. It also listed the annual report and next year's work plans for eight city commissions.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a proposed amendment to the design services agreement with Callander Associates Landscape Architecture for the Metro Tango Subdistrict Park Project, with a cap of $130,000.

The agenda listed a resolution to rename the Cesar Chavez Community Garden the "Milpitas Community Garden" and Cesar Chavez Plaza the "Milpitas Civic Center Plaza," and to name the community garden in Delano Manongs Park the "Larry Itliong Community Garden."
The agenda listed a presentation from the Santa Clara County Mosquito and Vector Control District.

The agenda listed acceptance of the FY2025-26 Commission Annual Report and approval of FY2026-27 work plans for eight commissions, including the Arts Commission, the Economic Development and Trade Commission, and the Library and Education Advisory Commission.

The agenda listed routine items: the October and November 2026 meeting calendar, the October 6, 2026 minutes, a preview of items for the next regular meeting, and the list of items requested by Councilmembers.

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Architectural Review Board — October 15, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The agenda listed a public hearing before Palo Alto's Architectural Review Board on a request from AT&T to add new wireless equipment to two existing city-owned wood utility poles in the public right-of-way. The poles are near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue.
keyTopics: AT&T's request (file 26PLN-00229) to add new antennas, remote radio units, and associated equipment to two existing city-owned wood utility poles, treated as two Tier 2 wireless communication facilities
Proposed seven-foot fiberglass pole extensions on the poles, located near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue
Listed as a quasi-judicial public hearing, with the project marked exempt from environmental review under CEQA Section 15301 (Existing Facilities)
A supplemental report was added to the agenda packet for this item
